transcript:
Meeting header:
- Date: 2025-10-06
- Time: 16:00 UTC / 09:00 PT
- Duration: 52 minutes
- Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE), Ethan Monroe (Redwood SE), Lina Osei (Redwood CSM), Ravi Desai (CTO, Autumn Ridge), Sophie Klein (Platform Eng), Carlos Mendez (Security), Nora Liang (DevOps)

Summary:
Quick onboarding launch to hand off access, confirm networking and security checklist, align on pilot success criteria and timing for Dedicated vs Hosted evaluation. Confirmed next steps around VPC details and SOC2 artifacts; SE to run baseline latency tests with customer sample payloads.

Topics Covered:
- Access & onboarding steps (API keys, service accounts, roles)
- VPC / private deployment constraints and IP allowlist
- Security requirements (audit logs, KMS, SSO/SAML)
- Pilot scope, success criteria, and timeline
- Cost and capacity discussion (dedicated pool vs hosted)

Action items reviewed at end.

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya (Redwood): hey everyone thanks for carving out time, um this is Maya from Redwood, i'll run quick intro - Ethan's our solutions engineer, Lina's your CSM. we wanted to make this a hands-on launch so we can unblock the pilot this month.

[00:28] Ravi (Autumn Ridge): yeah thanks maya, appreciate it. we have a few constraints up front — data residency, we need everything in eu-west-1 for now, and security wants audit logs for every inference request.

[00:46] Ethan (Redwood): got it, eu-west-1 pinning's doable for Hosted and also for Private deploys; for Dedicated we can reserve a pool in that region. quick q: are you leaning on VPC peering, or do you prefer a strictly private on-prem box?

[01:10] Sophie (Autumn Ridge): we're planning to start with VPC peering into our Azure tenancy, but long term we may want an on-prem option for certain PHI flows. for the pilot we'll do VPC.

[01:34] Carlos (Autumn Ridge): and on the security side, KMS integration is mandatory, and we need to map RBAC to our SAML groups. also, can you retain audit logs for 12 months?

[01:57] Lina (Redwood): quick note — Redwood supports KMS and HSM integrations in Private; for Hosted we have customer-managed keys via our KMS connector. retention windows are configurable via the console, we should capture exact retention SLA in the security doc.

[02:20] Maya (Redwood): ok let's outline onboarding steps: 1) we'll provision service account and initial API key scoped to pilot; 2) SE will share VPC/network checklist; 3) customer shares sample payloads and traffic profile; 4) run baseline tests; 5) review results and decide dedicated vs hosted.

[02:48] Nora (Autumn Ridge): on sample payloads — we have two flows: short chat prompts and a batch of enrichment embeddings. can you support both? there might be token size variance.

[03:06] Ethan (Redwood): yes both are supported. for embeddings we stream smaller batches to avoid cold starts; for chat we recommend continuous batching and prefix cache. small note: our KV cache sometimes gets transcribed as K V cash in our internal notes — sorry, bad joke.

[03:30] Ravi (Autumn Ridge): ha, noted. what's redo latency on the chat path? we need p95 sub 220ms for 2k token context?

[03:50] Ethan (Redwood): p95 depends on model and whether you use quantized variants. for a 2k context on a medium-sized model on Dedicated, p95 ~ 180-250ms typical; Hosted has more variance during peak. we'll run a baseline with your payloads to show numbers.

[04:20] Carlos (Autumn Ridge): about encryption — do you support envelope encryption with customer KMS? and can we rotate keys monthly?

[04:38] Lina (Redwood): yes, envelope encryption with customer-managed KMS is supported on Private and Dedicated; Hosted supports customer KMS via connector, rotation cadence can be configured, we usually recommend 30/90 days depending on policy.

[04:58] Sophie (Autumn Ridge): network side: what's the egress pattern? we need to know IP ranges to allowlist.

[05:12] Ethan (Redwood): we'll provide a stable prefix set for Dedicated and a published list for Hosted; for pilot we'll give a short list to allowlist. i'll attach that to the VPC checklist.

[05:30] Ravi (Autumn Ridge): can we do canary model rollouts? we want A/B between a higher-quality model and a cheaper quantized model to control cost.

[05:46] Ethan (Redwood): absolutely — rollouts and traffic split are in the Console. you can route by percentage and set automatic fallback to the higher-tier model if latency breaches. for cost-savings we suggest caching hot prefixes and using model quantization where quality holds.

[06:10] Nora (Autumn Ridge): what's the uptick on logging? we want per-token cost breakdowns in analytics for our product team.

[06:25] Lina (Redwood): Console shows token counts, cost per route, and token-level breakdown. we can set retention and connect to your SIEM for long-term storage.

[06:44] Maya (Redwood): quick preflight on pilot scope: 2-week pilot, two routes (chat and embeddings), regional pin to eu-west-1, success criteria: p95 latency under 250ms for chat, embeddings throughput X qps (customer to provide), and no unresolved security issues. is that ok?

[07:04] Ravi (Autumn Ridge): yes that's fine. we also want an operational runbook for incident response — who to page and escalation path.

[07:18] Maya (Redwood): Lina will own runbook draft and we'll share a first pass within 3 business days.

[07:30] Ethan (Redwood): for the baseline tests i'll need a small set of 50 chat prompts and 500 embedding inputs to run p95/throughput tests. share them in the shared folder or via the secure upload link.

[07:46] Sophie (Autumn Ridge): we'll sanitize and upload by end of day tomorrow. note: some prompts include shorthand and product names that can trip redaction, expect slight edits.

[08:00] Carlos (Autumn Ridge): small heads up — our compliance team will want to run an SSO test and a sample audit log review before we go live. do you have a standard pack?

[08:15] Lina (Redwood): yes, we have a security pack: SOC2 attestation, sample audit logs, KMS integration guide, SAML SSO flow doc. i'll send the pack after the call.

[08:28] Maya (Redwood): moving to cost briefly — i'll share both a hosted cost projection and a dedicated reserved capacity model. dedicated gives predictable unit cost and lower p95 variance, hosted is quicker to start.

[08:46] Ravi (Autumn Ridge): timeline-wise we need pilot results by end of October to inform Q4 procurement decisions. can we aim to start the pilot week of 2025-10-20?

[09:02] Maya (Redwood): yes that aligns. to hit that date: we need VPC checklist completed and sample payloads in by 2025-10-13, and security docs by 2025-10-09. we'll draft a calendar invite for the pilot kickoff.

[09:20] Ethan (Redwood): quick technical note: if you plan to use large context windows we recommend the model variants with KV cache support; otherwise cost grows and latency may spike. sometimes our transcriber writes KV cache as K V cash in notes which looks odd later.

[09:40] Sophie (Autumn Ridge): about metrics — do you expose per-request traces we can correlate with our APM?

[09:52] Ethan (Redwood): yes, we provide trace IDs and hooks for OpenTelemetry. we can instrument and show sample traces in the Console during the baseline run.

[10:08] Nora (Autumn Ridge): ok last thing — who is the single technical contact for the pilot? i'd like a single Slack channel and pager on rotation.

[10:20] Maya (Redwood): we'll set up a dedicated slack channel. primary contacts: Ethan for infra/latency, Lina for onboarding and ops, Maya for contract/pricing. we'll include on-call rotation details in the runbook.

[10:38] Ravi (Autumn Ridge): great. anything else from your side?

[10:45] Ethan (Redwood): just to confirm deliverables: i'll send the VPC checklist, run the baseline test and share results; Lina will send security pack and runbook draft; Maya will share cost spreadsheet and contract addendum.

[11:02] Carlos (Autumn Ridge): and we'll provide sample payloads, IP allowlist, and SOC2 scope.

[11:15] Maya (Redwood): perfect. recap of next steps then — we'll email notes and action items; target pilot kickoff week of 2025-10-20. thanks all.

[11:28] (Call ends)

Notes on transcription: occasional mis-hearings (K V cash, transcriber sporadic punctuation). speakers sometimes overlap briefly.
